scope: Batch review of R14, A01, A02, A03, A04 only. Read all of app/, config/, deploy/k8s/, release/manifest.yaml, migrations/001_init.sql, Dockerfile, .github/workflows/ci.yaml, prompts and README. Ran prescan (7 hits, all for B07/B08/B09/B11/R05, none for this batch) and the inventory. No .brace/ directory found. Not reviewed: other items, STS/IAM/RBAC policy outside the repo, tests. Code was not executed. Model: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5), default reasoning. Challenges were not run (fresh process to do that). Normal mode, no --conservative.

findings.title: Distinct agent identity
findings.requirement: Give the agent its own verifiable non-human identity, separate from the user who launched it and from unrelated agents. Preserve any explicitly delegated user/system subject separately and bound the authority used. Show that operators can revoke the agent's access independently of that subject, even when a user starts the run.

not_covered.problem: Action records missing any of the six identity fields
Instance or tenant labels taken from what the model supplies
A credential scoped to more operations, resources, or tenants than needed
Revocation delay from cached or self-contained tokens not measured

evidence.note: Exchanged-token cache is keyed by audience, scope and tenant only. A token minted for one user's delegation is reused for other users in the tenant, so the delegated subject does not survive per call.

checks.check: The agent runs under its own workload principal (service account, IAM role, SPIFFE ID, or agent ID) that no other service or unrelated agent uses.
checks.verify: 1) Find the agent's identity: pod `serviceAccountName`, IAM role, SPIFFE ID, or agent ID in IaC or deploy config. 2) Search other deployments, services, and agents in the repo for the same name or role. 3) Answer no if it is shared, `default`, the main backend's identity, or only a string label with no credential. Answer unknown if identity is assigned outside this repo.
checks.counter_search: Searched deploy/k8s, release/manifest.yaml and app/ for other serviceAccountName values, default SA use and other workloads sharing procurement-agent; only this one Deployment exists.
checks.note: Pod runs under its own service account; token is projected and exchanged at the STS.

coverage.subject: procurement-agent pod identity
coverage.note: Deployment uses a dedicated named service account, not default.

coverage.subject: service account object
coverage.note: Dedicated ServiceAccount defined for this agent only.

coverage.subject: agent principal string
coverage.note: Audit rows carry the same SPIFFE principal as the service account.

coverage.subject: extractor sub-agent
coverage.note: Child identity copies the parent principal; it is the same agent, not an unrelated one.

checks.check: Tool and API clients use short-lived credentials with a verified acting-agent identity and any separately bounded user/system delegation; they do not copy a login session or reuse a gateway token at a different backend audience.
checks.verify: 1) Trace every client credential to its issuer, audience, acting principal and delegated subject. 2) Accept authorized OAuth delegation and supported exchange when agent identity and bounded grants survive. 3) Reject copied sessions, shared static keys, or cross-audience token reuse. 4) Mark issuer/downstream guarantees unknown if only external evidence can show them.
checks.note: Exchanged-token cache is keyed by audience, scope and tenant only. A token minted for one user's delegation is reused for other users in the tenant, so the delegated subject does not survive per call.

checks.check: For user-initiated runs, the original user is a verified delegated subject while the acting agent retains its own principal.
checks.verify: 1) Trace user-started runs and credential issuance, including OAuth delegation and token exchange where supported. 2) Check original subject, acting agent and granted task/tenant/resource limits independently. 3) Reject a user label from model-controlled input or replacement of agent identity with a human session. 4) For machine-only operation, cite the configuration showing there is no delegated user; do not invent one.
checks.note: The user is sent to the STS as a bare subject-id string typed urn:example:params:subject-id, not as a verified user token. The STS cannot verify the user from this request; the user's JWT is verified only at /runs (app/main.py:126).

checks.check: Permissions are bound to the agent principal in IaC or RBAC, so revoking that principal alone removes the agent's access without disabling the user.
checks.verify: 1) Find IAM policies, RoleBindings, or grants in Terraform, Helm, or Kubernetes YAML. 2) Check they bind to the agent principal, not to a user, group, or shared role. 3) Check that removing that binding alone would cut the agent's access. 4) Answer no if revoking the agent cannot remove its access independently, or authority uses a shared credential. User grants may legitimately bound an explicitly delegated flow. Answer unknown if permissions are not defined in this repo.
checks.note: No IAM policy, RoleBinding or STS grant mapping is defined in this repo. Only a ServiceAccount (deploy/k8s/serviceaccount.yaml) and DB grants to role procurement_agent (migrations/001_init.sql:119-128) exist. STS authorization for the SPIFFE ID lives outside the repo.

violates: Preserve any explicitly delegated user/system subject separately and bound the authority used
findings.summary: Token exchange drops per-user delegation (shared cache) and sends the user only as an unverified label.
findings.next_step: Key the token cache on the delegated subject, and send a verified user token or signed delegation to the STS. Show the STS grants for the agent principal.

findings.title: All six identity fields
findings.requirement: Check that every action records the accountable party, operational owner, tenant, agent-type-id, agent-instance-id, and trace context. Look at successful, denied, failed, and background actions, not just the main request path.

not_covered.problem: Identity labels taken from what the model supplies
Agent-type-id not computed as a hash of its identity inputs
Agent able to erase or rewrite its own audit history
Sub-agent record missing its parent link or parent prompt

evidence.note: A halted run raises AgentHalted before any audit record is written. run_halted is defined (audit.py:27) but never recorded. reserve_run_start (loop.py:129) raising BudgetExceeded is outside the try block, so quota refusals write nothing. The Slack approval decision (main.py:183) and /ingest/mail also write no audit record, and auth failures return 401/403 unlogged.

checks.check: The audit record schema has all six fields: accountable party, operational owner, tenant, agent-type-id, agent-instance-id, and trace context.
checks.verify: 1) Find the audit record schema or the function that writes audit entries. 2) Check for each of the six: accountable party, operational owner, tenant, `agent.type.id`, `agent.instance.id`, trace context (`traceparent` or trace and span IDs). 3) Answer no if any one is missing from the schema or never set.
checks.counter_search: Searched for other INSERT INTO audit_events or alternate writers; only audit.record writes the table.
checks.note: INSERT writes accountable party, owner, tenant, agent_type_id, agent_instance_id, trace_id and span_id; migration makes each NOT NULL and non-empty.

coverage.subject: accountable_party / operational_owner / tenant
coverage.note: All three are columns in the single audit INSERT.

coverage.subject: agent_type_id / agent_instance_id
coverage.note: Type and instance ids are columns in the same INSERT.

coverage.subject: trace context
coverage.note: trace_id is passed into the INSERT for every record.

coverage.subject: empty value guard
coverage.note: record() raises if any identity field is empty before writing.

coverage.subject: schema constraints
coverage.note: DB rejects empty values for the identity columns.

checks.check: All six fields are written on denied, failed, async, and background actions too, not only on the successful main request path.
checks.verify: 1) List every path that writes an audit record, or should: success, policy deny, `except`/`catch` blocks, retries, queue workers, cron jobs, webhooks, other endpoints such as approvals, and refusals before the run starts (quota, rate limit, auth) that return an error without logging. 2) For each, check all six fields are set, ideally by one shared wrapper. 3) Answer no if any deny, error, async, or background path writes records without them, or writes no record at all.
checks.note: A halted run raises AgentHalted before any audit record is written. run_halted is defined (audit.py:27) but never recorded. reserve_run_start (loop.py:129) raising BudgetExceeded is outside the try block, so quota refusals write nothing. The Slack approval decision (main.py:183) and /ingest/mail also write no audit record, and auth failures return 401/403 unlogged.

checks.check: Trace context (trace and span IDs) is stored in the audit record itself, not only in separate tracing spans.
checks.verify: 1) Open the audit record writer. 2) Check it stores trace and span IDs (or `traceparent`) as fields in the record itself. 3) Answer no if trace context exists only in OpenTelemetry spans, or the record's trace field is never filled.
checks.counter_search: Searched for paths where trace_id is unset: RunIdentity.__post_init__ rejects an empty trace_id (identity.py:47). span_id is nullable when no span is active (audit.py:90).
checks.note: trace_id and span_id are stored as columns of audit_events; trace_id is NOT NULL.

coverage.subject: trace_id column
coverage.note: trace_id from the identity is written into the record itself.

coverage.subject: span_id column
coverage.note: span_id from the active span is written into the record.

coverage.subject: trace_id never empty
coverage.note: Identity creation fails if trace_id is empty.

checks.check: Tenant and owner values come from the trusted layer, not from baggage, tracestate, or other unprotected headers.
checks.verify: 1) Find where tenant and owner values for audit records are read. 2) Trace each back to its source: token claims, verified session, IAM tags, or SPIFFE path, versus OTel baggage, `tracestate`, headers like `X-Tenant-Id`, request body, or tool arguments. 3) Answer no if any path takes them from an unprotected source.
checks.counter_search: Searched audit writers and RunIdentity constructors for X-Tenant, baggage, tracestate, request body and tool-argument sources; none feed tenant or owner.
checks.note: Tenant comes from the 'bu' claim of a verified RS256/ES256 JWT; owner comes from deployment settings; background jobs use fixed values.

coverage.subject: run tenant
coverage.note: Tenant taken from verified token claim bu.

coverage.subject: token verification
coverage.note: Claims are only read after signature, audience and issuer checks.

coverage.subject: run owner
coverage.note: Owner comes from environment settings, not the request.

coverage.subject: background tenant/owner
coverage.note: Background identity uses a fixed system tenant and settings owner.

coverage.subject: sub-agent identity
coverage.note: Child identity inherits tenant and owner from the parent identity.

red_flags_found: app/loop.py:127 Pre-run refusals (kill switch, run-start quota) and approval decisions write no audit record.
violates: every action records the accountable party
findings.summary: The six fields are in the record schema, but denied-at-start and approval paths write no audit record.
findings.next_step: Record run_halted, quota refusals, approval decisions, ingest and auth rejections through audit.record with full identity.

findings.title: Content-derived type identity
findings.requirement: Compute the agent-type-id as a hash of the container digest, harness, system prompt, model ID and version, and configuration. The model part includes checkpoint and fine-tune or adapter references where they apply. Keep the list of inputs (the manifest) and the hashing steps. Check that changing any input changes the ID, and that the same manifest gives the same ID.

not_covered.problem: Changed running config still reporting the old approved ID
Hosted model changing behind a fixed name
Release manifest missing training job, dataset, or model provider records
Action records missing any of the six identity fields

evidence.note: Only the prompt file path is hashed, not its content hash, so editing prompts/system.md does not change the agent-type-id. The extractor prompt has the same flaw (identity.py:69).

checks.check: The agent-type-id is a hash over a manifest that includes the container digest, harness, system prompt, model ID and version, and configuration.
checks.verify: 1) Find the code or CI step that computes `agent.type.id` (search `sha256`, `hashlib`, `createHash`, `type_id`). 2) List its inputs. 3) Check each is there: container digest, harness, system prompt, model ID and version, configuration. 4) Answer no if the ID is a label, version string, or git tag, or any input is missing.
checks.note: Only the prompt file path is hashed, not its content hash, so editing prompts/system.md does not change the agent-type-id. The extractor prompt has the same flaw (identity.py:69).

checks.check: The hash covers every file that defines the prompt, tools, and configuration, with no file or directory skipped or excluded.
checks.verify: 1) Open the function that lists files to hash. 2) Write down every filter it applies: hidden files, names starting with '_' or '__', extensions, ignore lists, glob patterns. 3) For each filter, check whether a file that defines tools, prompts, or config would be skipped (for example `__init__.py`, `index.ts`, `.env`, `config/*.local.*`). 4) Answer no if any such file is skipped.
checks.note: Prompt file contents are not in the hash. Startup only logs when running files differ from the manifest (startup.py:43), so the ID can describe files that are not the running ones.

checks.check: The model input is a pinned version or snapshot (plus checkpoint and adapter references where used), not an alias and not the app's release number.
checks.verify: 1) Find the model ID that goes into the manifest or hash. 2) Follow env vars and config to the final value, including defaults such as `getenv('MODEL', ...)`. 3) Answer no if it is an alias (`-latest`, no date or version), falls back to one when unset, or is the app release number. Also no if adapters or checkpoints are used but left out.
checks.counter_search: Searched settings.py and deployment.yaml for aliases and fallbacks: _env('MODEL_ID') has no default and deployment pins the same snapshot.
checks.note: Both models are dated snapshots in the hashed manifest; adapter and fine_tune are none; MODEL_ID has no default.

coverage.subject: primary model
coverage.note: Primary model is a dated snapshot in the hashed manifest.

coverage.subject: extractor model
coverage.note: Extractor model is a dated snapshot in the hashed manifest.

coverage.subject: runtime model env
coverage.note: No default value, so no alias fallback when unset.

coverage.subject: adapters
coverage.note: No adapter or checkpoint is used so none is omitted.

checks.check: The manifest is put in a fixed, documented order before hashing, so the same manifest always gives the same ID.
checks.verify: 1) Open the serialization step before hashing. 2) Check for a fixed order: sorted keys (`sort_keys=True`), sorted file lists, fixed encoding and line endings. 3) Check file lists are not taken straight from directory listing or map iteration order. 4) Answer no if any unsorted dict, map, or filesystem order reaches the hash.
checks.counter_search: Searched for file listings or unsorted iteration reaching the hash; the input is a dict built from YAML values only.
checks.note: Manifest material is serialized with sorted keys, fixed separators and utf-8 encoding before sha256.

coverage.subject: serialization
coverage.note: Sorted keys and fixed separators give a deterministic string.

coverage.subject: encoding
coverage.note: Fixed utf-8 encoding is used before hashing.

checks.check: Secret values are not placed in the hashed manifest in a form that exposes them.
checks.verify: 1) List every value fed into the manifest or hash. 2) Check whether any are secrets: API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, `.env` contents. 3) Answer no if a secret value is written in plain text to the stored manifest, or the whole environment is dumped into it.
checks.counter_search: Read release/manifest.yaml and compute_agent_type_id inputs for tokens, keys and passwords; none present.
checks.note: Hashed inputs are digests, paths, model ids, config hashes and tool pins; no credentials or environment dump.

coverage.subject: hash material
coverage.note: Material is built from named manifest entries, not os.environ.

coverage.subject: manifest content
coverage.note: Manifest holds public digests and ids, no secret values.

red_flags_found: app/startup.py:43 Mismatch between running state and manifest is logged, not refused; the type id is computed from the manifest anyway.
violates: hash of the container digest, harness, system prompt
findings.summary: The type id hashes prompt file paths, not their contents, and a manifest mismatch is only logged.
findings.next_step: Hash the prompt sha256 values and every tool and config file digest. Refuse to start when running files differ from the manifest.

findings.title: Trustworthy attribution
findings.requirement: Assign instance and tenant identity in the trusted execution layer. Don't accept labels the model supplies. Record the delegated subject — the user or system whose authority is being used — separately from the agent's identity. Test that the agent can't pose as another instance or tenant in requests or audit records. Test that trace context survives handoffs between async jobs. Treat trace IDs and caller-supplied labels only as a way to link records. They never prove identity or permission.

not_covered.problem: Agent sharing the launching user's identity
Prompt a parent gave a sub-agent not recorded
Sub-agent authorized using an earlier actor's authority
Action records missing any of the six identity fields

evidence.note: memory_read uses the model-supplied business_unit as the tenant to read from. The tool schema offers the field (memory.py:113). Other tools use ident.tenant.

checks.check: Tenant and instance identity are set by the harness or platform from verified context, never from model-produced text or tool arguments.
checks.verify: 1) Find every place tenant and instance IDs are set for tool calls and records. 2) Check each comes from verified context (token claims, session bound at launch). 3) Check tool JSON schemas the model fills for `tenant_id`, `user_id`, `instance_id`. 4) Answer no if any function uses the model's value, even if another function uses verified context.
checks.note: memory_read uses the model-supplied business_unit as the tenant to read from. The tool schema offers the field (memory.py:113). Other tools use ident.tenant.

checks.check: Tenant or instance labels in tool arguments or agent-controlled headers are rejected or overwritten with the verified values before they are used or logged.
checks.verify: 1) Find tool handlers and middleware that receive tool arguments and headers. 2) Check that tenant or instance fields in arguments, or headers like `X-Tenant-Id`, are rejected or overwritten with the verified value before use or logging. 3) Answer no if any handler uses or logs the supplied value, or detects a mismatch and continues.
checks.note: The supplied tenant label is used in the query rather than rejected or overwritten with ident.tenant. erp_call does overwrite it (erp.py:26).

checks.check: The delegated subject is recorded separately from the agent identity.
checks.verify: 1) Open the audit record schema and writer. 2) Look for a delegated-subject field (the user or system whose authority is used) separate from the agent principal field. 3) Answer no if only one identity is stored, the user overwrites the agent identity, or the field is never filled.
checks.counter_search: Searched for paths where delegated_subject is empty or replaces agent_principal; main.py:155-156 sets both, service_identity sets a system subject.
checks.note: delegated_subject and agent_principal are separate columns, filled from the verified JWT sub and the SPIFFE id.

coverage.subject: delegated subject column
coverage.note: Delegated subject written as its own column.

coverage.subject: agent principal column
coverage.note: Agent principal stored separately from the subject.

coverage.subject: run start
coverage.note: Subject taken from verified token sub claim.

coverage.subject: agent principal at start
coverage.note: Agent principal is a constant, not the user.

coverage.subject: background run
coverage.note: System subject is recorded for background jobs.

checks.check: When work is handed to an async job or queue, the trusted layer attaches the verified attribution and trace context, and the job uses them.
checks.verify: 1) Find queue producers and enqueue calls (Celery, SQS, Pub/Sub, Kafka, cron). 2) Check the trusted layer adds verified identity and trace context to the job. 3) Check the worker uses those values, not ones the agent wrote. 4) Answer no if workers start new traces without parent context or take tenant from agent-written job data.
checks.counter_search: Searched for celery, sqs, kafka, pubsub, queue and cron producers; none exist. The approval sweeper (main.py:110) starts a fresh system identity with no inbound context to propagate.
checks.note: The only handoff is an in-process task started with the harness-built identity, which carries tenant and trace_id; sub-agents inherit via child().

coverage.subject: run task handoff
coverage.note: Task receives the verified identity object, not agent-written data.

coverage.subject: sub-agent handoff
coverage.note: Child identity keeps tenant and trace_id and records the parent instance.

coverage.subject: approval sweeper
coverage.note: Fresh system identity for a timer job; there is no inbound request context.

checks.check: Authorization never treats trace IDs or caller-supplied labels as proof of identity or permission.
checks.verify: 1) Find authorization and permission-lookup code. 2) Check what each decision is keyed on. 3) Answer no if any check uses a trace ID, span ID, correlation ID, request label, or caller-supplied header as identity or to look up permissions.
checks.note: memory_read looks up which tenant's notes are returned from a caller-supplied business_unit label, with no permission check. The tool description says shared-services staff may do this, but nothing verifies that.

red_flags_found: app/tools/memory.py:44 memory_read takes the tenant from model-controlled arguments and reads another business unit's notes.
violates: Don't accept labels the model supplies
findings.summary: memory_read accepts a model-supplied tenant label and uses it to choose whose notes to return.
findings.next_step: Remove business_unit from the memory_read schema and always use ident.tenant. If cross-unit reads are needed, add a verified entitlement check.

findings.title: Recovery integrity
findings.requirement: If logs or checkpoints drive recovery, make them tamper-evident. Before using them, verify them against a separately protected trust anchor or signing key. Test that verification rejects changed checkpoints. It must also catch truncation, rollback to an older valid checkpoint, and replacement of a whole hash chain. For automatic recovery, confirm the destination supports idempotency: sending the same request twice has the effect of sending it once. Replay only within the destination's documented scope and time window. Confirm that actions you can't undo don't happen twice. Where support is missing or the result is unclear, check that replay pauses for reconciliation instead of sending again.

not_covered.problem: What happens to in-flight writes and queued actions at stop
Rollback to an approved earlier release not tested
Agent able to delete or rewrite its own audit history

evidence.note: audit_events is only inserted into; no code in app/ reads it to recover or replay
runs are in-memory asyncio tasks; nothing resumes or replays them after a restart

checks.check: Checkpoints and audit records used for recovery are hash-chained or signed.
checks.verify: 1) Find checkpoint and audit storage used for recovery. 2) Check for hash chaining or signatures. 3) Answer no if records are plain rows or files with no chain or signature.
checks.note: audit_events is insert-only here; no code reads audit rows or checkpoints to drive recovery (grep for checkpoint, replay, resume, recover found nothing).

checks.check: Recovery verifies them against a key or trust anchor stored separately from the records, and refuses any that fail.
checks.verify: 1) Find recovery code that loads checkpoints. 2) Check it verifies against a key stored separately and refuses failures. 3) Answer no if the key sits in the same store, verification is skipped, or failure is logged and recovery continues.
checks.note: No recovery path loads logs or checkpoints, so there is nothing to verify.

checks.check: Verification catches truncation, rollback to an older valid checkpoint, and replacement of the whole chain, for example with a signed head or sequence number held outside the store.
checks.verify: 1) Check verification uses a signed head or sequence number held outside the store. 2) Answer no if truncation, rollback to an older valid checkpoint, or replacing the whole chain would still pass.
checks.note: No recovery path loads logs or checkpoints, so there is nothing to verify.

checks.check: Automatic replay sends idempotency keys that the destination enforces, and only for integrations that support them.
checks.verify: 1) Find replay code. 2) Check it sends idempotency keys (`Idempotency-Key`, `client_token`) only to integrations that enforce them. 3) Answer no if replay sends without keys, uses a local dedupe table as the only guard, or replays to integrations without support.
checks.note: No automatic replay exists. pay_invoice sends an Idempotency-Key (payments.py:33) only on the model's own call.

checks.check: When idempotency is missing or the result is unclear, replay pauses for reconciliation instead of resending.
checks.verify: 1) Find replay handling for unclear results or missing idempotency. 2) Answer no if replay resends instead of pausing for reconciliation, or retry is the default on timeout.
checks.note: No automatic replay exists. Runs are in-memory asyncio tasks (main.py:159) and are not resumed after restart.

findings.summary: No logs or checkpoints drive recovery and nothing replays automatically.
findings.next_step: Governance to confirm. Re-open if run resume or replay from audit_events is added.
